hospital_course: You came to the emergency department with burning when you urinate, urgency, and lower belly discomfort. Your urine test showed infection and your kidneys were not involved. You were observed overnight, given fluids, and started on an oral antibiotic.

medications.name: Nitrofurantoin
medications.note: Take it with meals to reduce stomach upset.

diet: Drink 6 to 8 cups (1.5 to 2 liters) of water a day to help flush your bladder.
Limit caffeine and alcohol while you recover because they can irritate the bladder.
activity: You may return to normal activity as you feel able.
Urinate when you feel the urge and do not hold it. Empty your bladder after sex.
care: A warm heating pad on your lower belly may ease discomfort.
monitoring: Notice whether the burning improves within 2 days of starting the antibiotic.
Check your temperature each evening for 3 days.

follow_up.purpose: a follow-up visit and urine recheck if symptoms continue

warning_signs: shaking chills with a fast heartbeat
call_clinic: fever of 101 F (38.3 C) or higher
pain in your back or side
vomiting so you cannot keep the antibiotic down
